title: Analyze a Simulated Access-Control Incident
summary: Integrate synthetic identity, access, physical, log, evidence, and escalation reasoning.
objectives: Analyze a synthetic cyber and physical access scenario.
Document known facts, uncertainty, safe action, and escalation.

vocab.def: An event affecting or threatening normal operations that requires an authorized response.
The systems, data, and actions included in an authorized task.
Passing a concern to an authorized person or team.

sections.heading: Scenario packet
sections.body: Use synthetic identities, roles, permissions, badge events, login events, permission changes, system alerts, and account lifecycle records. Not every clue proves malicious activity.

sections.heading: Simulation-only boundary
sections.body: Do not access real accounts, bypass controls, scan systems, crack passwords, deploy tools, alter logs, clone badges, evade cameras, or contain systems outside the scenario scope.

practice.prompt: An account is active after an expected departure and a permission change follows a badge event. What should the report contain?
practice.answer: Known timestamps and records, affected identity and scope, uncertainty, preserved sources, and authorized escalation.

quiz.question: What is the correct response to an unauthorized action request?
options: Stop, preserve evidence, document, and escalate
quiz.answer: Stop, preserve evidence, document, and escalate

criteria: Chooses authorized next steps and escalation

lab.objective: Analyze and document a synthetic access-control incident.

futureCompetencyCandidates: document and escalate a simulated security incident
reflectionPrompt: Which action did you deliberately avoid because it exceeded authorization?
